To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified 5 Japanese ALS patients with OPTN deletion mutations, which were previously unknown.
we identified 3 kinds (one homozygous and two heterozygous) of novel OPTN deletions in 3.5% of Japanese ALS.
we identified three kinds of novel deletion mutations in OPTN in Japanese amyotrophic lateral sclerosiss (ALS).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel deletion mutation of the OPTN gene in ALS.
the development of a novel screening system for the OPTN deletional mutations and the prevalence of OPTN mutations in Japanese ALS patients.
a new method for detecting mutations in the OPTN gene and the prevalence of OPTN mutation in ALS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
4% of familial and approximately 1% of sporadic Japanese ALS are caused by OPTN mutations.
the OPTN mutation is responsible for at least 5.3% of ALS, and that the OPTN gene is the second most common disease gene in ALS after SOD1.
the OPTN mutations in Japanese ALS are 4.2% of familial and at least 0.7% of sporadic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
4.5% of ALS in Japanese are caused by OPTN mutations, which is the highest prevalence among all ALS genes.
the OPTN deletional mutation in Japanese ALS is not infrequently observed, and the prevalence of OPTN mutation in sporadic ALS is high.
the OPTN mutation is responsible for 3.8-6.7% of familial and up to 1.4% of sporadic Japanese ALS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
OPTN mutations are not infrequent in ALS.
we identified three new deletions in five patients with ALS, which are expected to result from null alleles.
the prevalence of OPTN mutation in ALS may be underestimated.
